name: Animal Industry Careers & Ethics

objectives.text: Name people who work with animals, such as a farmer, veterinarian, and 4-H or FFA member, and tell one job each person does
Describe why it is important to treat farm animals with care and respect
Explain what it means for an animal caretaker to be a good steward of the animals and resources entrusted to them
Explain the responsibilities of animal science careers, such as veterinarian, livestock nutritionist, or farm manager
Identify the Five Freedoms of animal welfare and give an example of how a caretaker meets each one
Identify the employability skills animal industry employers value, such as work ethic, communication, and safe animal handling
Classify career pathways in the animal industry by the level of education, training, and certification each requires
Distinguish between animal welfare and animal rights viewpoints and explain how each shapes beliefs about the use of animals
Summarize the major segments of the animal industry, such as livestock, companion animal, research, and aquaculture, and the careers found in each
Develop a supervised agricultural experience plan in animal science that connects to a chosen career interest and includes goals and record keeping
Explain how laws and agencies such as the USDA, APHIS, FDA, and the Animal Welfare Act regulate the care and use of animals
Analyze the economic contribution of animal industry sectors to local and state economies and the employment they support
Analyze a current ethical issue in animal agriculture, such as housing systems or antibiotic use, from multiple stakeholder perspectives
Apply a professional code of conduct, such as the veterinarian's oath or a livestock exhibition ethics code, to a case involving animal care or show ring practices
Evaluate how welfare audits and quality assurance programs such as Beef Quality Assurance influence production practices and consumer confidence in animal products
Analyze how media coverage and consumer perceptions shape public trust in animal agriculture and its practices
Create a speech or presentation that accurately explains an animal agriculture practice to a nonfarm audience
Develop a personal career plan for an animal industry pathway that includes education, certifications, SAE, and FFA experiences
Evaluate the ethical, economic, and stewardship considerations involved in a career decision or policy issue within the animal industry and justify a position

changes: Kept and lightly reworded all six existing objectives as real competencies. Added stewardship, the Five Freedoms, welfare versus rights, and employability skills in the middle grades. Added high school objectives on industry segments, SAE planning, regulation and agencies, economic impact, professional codes of conduct, quality assurance and audits, public perception, agricultural communication, and personal career planning. Aligned AFNR codes only where the objective teaches the standard, and left the lower grades without codes.
